title: Red shift and an expanding universe
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:57Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point is a Year 12 physics card that teaches Hubble's law quantitatively, with the formula v = H₀d, the Hubble constant, standard candles and megaparsec calculations, which is well beyond the qualitative Year 10 idea of red shift and an expanding universe, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Red shift and an expanding universe
card: Light travels as waves. Red light has a longer wavelength than blue light.
Light from distant galaxies is stretched to longer, redder wavelengths. This is called red shift.
Edwin Hubble found that the farther away a galaxy is, the more its light is red shifted. This means farther galaxies move away faster.
Galaxies moving away from us in every direction shows that the universe is expanding.
draft.remember: Red shift shows galaxies moving away, and farther ones move faster, so the universe is expanding.

a.q: What happens to the light from a galaxy that is moving away from us?
opts: Its wavelengths are stretched towards red
Its wavelengths are squeezed towards blue
Its light becomes brighter but keeps its colour
Its light changes colour only if it is close
a.why: Light from a galaxy moving away is stretched to longer, redder wavelengths. Squeezing towards blue would be the opposite, and it does not depend on the galaxy being close.
a.clue: Red light has a longer wavelength.

b.q: Galaxy X shows a larger red shift than Galaxy Y. What does Hubble's finding suggest about Galaxy X?
opts: It is farther away and moving away faster
It is closer and moving away faster
It is farther away and moving away slower
It is closer and moving away slower
b.why: Hubble found that more red shift goes with greater distance and greater speed of moving away. A closer galaxy would show less red shift, not more.
b.clue: More red shift means more distance.

a.best: Its wavelengths are stretched towards red

b.best: It is farther away and moving away faster
